scenes.narration: By the time Ehud Olmert reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. The son of a former Herut politician, Olmert was first elected to the Knesset for Likud in 1973, at the age of 28. Olmert served as a minister without portfolio from 1988 to 1990, and as Minister of Health from 1990 until 1992.

The rise of Ehud Olmert was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. He served two consecutive five-year terms before returning to national politics in 2003 to serve as Designated Acting Prime Minister, Minister of Trade and Minister of Communications. Olmert also served as acting Minister of Finance from 2005 to 2006, following the resignation of incumbent minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Setbacks came early for Ehud Olmert, and the response to them is the real story. In late 2005, Olmert joined Prime Minister Ariel Sharon in leaving Likud and forming Kadima alongside fellow Likud and Labor Party politicians. In January 2006, Olmert became the acting Prime Minister after Sharon was permanently incapacitated by a stroke.

The legacy of Ehud Olmert outlived the circumstances that produced it. Olmert went on to succeed Sharon as Kadima leader, and formed a government following elections held that March. During Olmert's term, Israel fought the 2006 Lebanon War, which ended inconclusively.

Few lives travel as far as that of Ehud Olmert, and the distance is the point. Olmert's approval dropped following the war, and he was harshly criticized for his handling of it by the Winograd Commission, whose findings prompted protests calling for his resignation. Olmert engaged in multiple rounds of peace talks with the Palestinians, including the 2007 Annapolis Conference, which ended following the breakout of the 2009 Gaza War.

The childhood of Ehud Olmert contains the adult in small print. Olmert resigned as prime minister in 2008 due to low approval ratings and a then-ongoing corruption probe. After leaving office, he was sentenced to six years in prison in 2014 for accepting bribes and for obstruction of justice during his terms as mayor of Jerusalem and as trade minister.

Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Ehud Olmert — in that order. Ehud Olmert was born in 1945 near Binyamina in the British Mandate of Palestine. According to Olmert, his parents, Bella Wagman and Mordechai Olmert, escaped persecution in Ukraine and Russia, and found sanctuary in Harbin, China.

The turning point in the life of Ehud Olmert looked like a failure at the time. His father Mordechai grew up in the city and was a member of its local Betar branch. Mordechai later became a politician and served as a member of the Knesset for Herut from 1955 to 1961.

Every biography of Ehud Olmert has to pass through the years that were quietly lost. In 2004, Olmert visited China and paid his respects at the tomb of his grandfather in Harbin. Olmert said that his father had never forgotten his Chinese hometown after moving to Palestine. "When he died at the age of 88, he spoke his last words in Mandarin Chinese", he recalled.

The education of Ehud Olmert happened mostly outside any school. Olmert graduated from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem with degrees in psychology, philosophy and law. He underwent many treatments, and later completed his military duties as a journalist for the IDF magazine BaMahane.

What Ehud Olmert wanted at the start and what Ehud Olmert got are not the same thing, and that gap is the story. During the Yom Kippur War, he joined the headquarters of Ariel Sharon as a military correspondent. Already a member of the Knesset, he decided to go through an officer's course in 1980 at the age of 35.

The defining trait of Ehud Olmert was not talent — it was the refusal to stop. The oldest daughter, Michal, holds a master's in psychology and leads workshops in creative thinking. Another daughter Dana is a lecturer in literature at the Tel Aviv University, the editor of a literature series, and a member of the Israeli human rights organization Machsom Watch.

Those who met Ehud Olmert at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. In 1966, Olmert, then head of the Gahal (a predecessor to Likud) student group at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, called for party leader Menachem Begin to step down during a party conference. Olmert was heckled by several attendees, but was applauded by Begin, who threatened to leave the conference if Olmert was not allowed to complete his speech.

The private years of Ehud Olmert explain the public decades better than any speech. That year, Olmert left Herut and joined the breakaway party Free Centre. Olmert was first elected to the Knesset in 1973 at the age of 28 as a member of Free Centre, now a faction within Likud.

The family Ehud Olmert came from matters more than the legends admit. Olmert was continuously re-elected to the Knesset as a member of Likud until 1998, when he resigned to avoid holding dual office while serving as Mayor of Jerusalem. In 1988, Olmert was appointed minister without portfolio responsible for minority affairs.

The first real success of Ehud Olmert arrived later than anyone expected, and changed everything. Following the dissolution of the twenty-third government, the Cabinet was reshuffled, and Olmert became the Minister of Health, serving until Likud's defeat in the 1992 election. In 1993, Olmert sought election as Mayor of Jerusalem, challenging longtime incumbent Teddy Kollek.

The last chapter of Ehud Olmert was written long after the fame. Olmert defeated Kollek by a large margin, becoming the first member of Likud or its precursors to hold the position. He resigned before the end of his term in February 2003, after being elected to another term in the Knesset.

The whole life of Ehud Olmert reads like a single decision repeated. During his term as mayor, he devoted himself to the initiation and advancement of major projects in the city, the development and improvement of the education system, and the development of road infrastructure. He also spearheaded the development of the light rail system in Jerusalem, and the investment of millions of shekels in the development of mass transportation options for the city.

Between the birth and the legend of Ehud Olmert lie the years that actually decide it. While mayor of Jerusalem, Olmert was an invited speaker at an international conflict resolution conference held in Derry, Northern Ireland. They are born because of differences in tradition and history; they are born because of differences in emotional, political and national circumstances.

The reputation of Ehud Olmert was built in the middle, not at the edges. If we are to overcome such fear, a credible and healthy political process must be carefully and painfully developed. Olmert returned to the Knesset as a member of Likud following the 2003 election. and was the chief negotiator behind the ensuing coalition agreement.

Somebody like Ehud Olmert should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. Following the elections he was appointed as Designated Acting Prime Minister and Minister of Industry, Trade and Labor. On 7 August 2005, Olmert was appointed acting finance minister, replacing Benjamin Netanyahu, who had resigned in protest against the planned Israeli withdrawal from the Gaza Strip.

The life of Ehud Olmert begins far from where the story usually starts. Olmert, who had originally opposed withdrawing from land captured in the Six-Day War, and who had voted against the Camp David Peace Accords in 1978, was a vocal supporter of the Gaza pullout. After his appointment, Olmert said:I voted against Menachem Begin, I told him it was a historic mistake, how dangerous it would be, and so on and so on.

Ehud Olmert was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. Now I am sorry he is not alive for me to be able to publicly recognize his wisdom and my mistake. Olmert left Likud in November 2005 to join Sharon's newly-formed Kadima party.

To understand where Ehud Olmert ended up, start with where Ehud Olmert began. On 4 January 2006, as the designated Acting Prime Minister, Olmert became Acting Prime Minister as a result of the serious stroke suffered by then Prime Minister Ariel Sharon. This occurred after consultations took place between Cabinet Secretary Yisrael Maimon and Attorney General Menachem Mazuz, who declared Sharon "temporarily incapable to carry out the duties of his office", while only officially in office.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Ehud Olmert ran through years nobody filmed. Then, Olmert and the cabinet reaffirmed in an announcement that the 28 March elections would be held as scheduled. During the days following the stroke, Olmert met with Shimon Peres and other Sharon supporters to try to convince them to stay with Kadima, rather than return to Likud or, in Peres' case, Labor.

Each stage of the life of Ehud Olmert made the next stage possible. On 16 January 2006, Olmert was elected chairman of Kadima, and Kadima's candidate for prime minister in the upcoming election. In his first major policy address on 24 January 2006 after becoming caretaker prime minister, Olmert stated that he backed the creation of a Palestinian state, and that Israel would have to relinquish parts of the West Bank to maintain its Jewish majority.

The people who knew Ehud Olmert young describe someone already restless. In the 2006 election, Kadima won 29 seats, making it the largest party. On 6 April, Olmert was officially asked by President Moshe Katsav to form a government.

What Ehud Olmert built in the middle years is what the name still stands for. Olmert had an initial period of 28 days to form a governing coalition, with a possible two-week extension. The 100-day replacement deadline was extended due to the Jewish festival of Passover, and a provision was made that, should Sharon's condition improve between 11 and 14 April, the declaration would not take effect.

By the time Ehud Olmert reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. Therefore, the official declaration took effect on 14 April, formally ending Sharon's term as prime minister and making Olmert the country's new Interim Prime Minister in office (he would not become the official prime minister until he formed a government). On 4 May 2006, Olmert presented his new government to the Knesset.
